result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.edge_percolation()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Simulate edge percolation by randomly removing edges. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L19369-L19422){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.edge_percolation( q, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Edge percolation](/assets/graphs/edge-percolation.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: the two diamonds sharing hub D. After removing 30 percent of the edges at random (here B–D, C–D, and D–E, drawn dashed), every node survives but the graph has split into the triangle A, B, C and the four nodes D, E, F, G." width="100%"} Creates a new graph with a fraction of edges randomly removed. All nodes are preserved. This is useful for analyzing network robustness under random edge failures or communication link failures. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [q]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Fraction of edges to remove (must be between `0.0` and `1.0`). For example, `q=0.2` removes 20% of edges. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph containing all nodes but only surviving edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Remove 50% of edges randomly: ::: {#eadd6fcf .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_full_graph(5) # K5 has 10 edges # Remove 50% of edges randomly percolated = graph.edge_percolation(q=0.5, seed=23) # Returns 5 - number of edges remaining after percolation percolated.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
